catalogStatus: Draft for owner review (issue #66). Not yet accepted as the complete acceptance contract.

I49.approval: Consolidates owner-approved decisions #30–#35; implementation plan not yet approved

I15.approval: Open owner questions; not a requirement source

fields.availability: Product availability from source inspection: available | partial | unavailable | unknown. Independent of verification. 'unavailable' means no implementation was found for an approved behavior; it is reported, not built, by verification work.
fields.automation: Verification readiness: executable (real Cucumber scenario) | missing-verification | blocked (prerequisite or owner decision absent).
fields.outcome: Run outcome is never stored here; it comes only from a run's result.json.
fields.supporting: Lower-level tests that support but do not replace story-level verification.

decisions.question: Which reference subject, trusted sources and versioned answer key/rubric should the tutor evaluation use, including approved good, bad and acceptable-variant examples for evaluator calibration?

Which evaluator model/configuration and which credential-holding processes may the initial live exercise use? The spec authorizes the bounded exercise but requires owner approval for any new credential access and an enforceable process/tool boundary before dispatch.

Which native Electron runtime and which physical iPhone/iPad Home Screen setups are available for target evidence? Issue #49 names laptop plus physical iPhone; the spec names Electron, iPhone and iPad. Confirm whether 'laptop' means native Electron.

How should learner and tutor move between teaching, practice, drills and review, how may the tutor prescribe a drill, and when should teaching revisit earlier capabilities? These are open in #15 and are not settled by this catalog.
What are on-demand check mechanics: scope selection, feedback timing and relationship to review scheduling? The vision leaves these to later decisions.
How do learner evidence and graph propositions relate for exploration? The vision requires domain alignment with upstream before design.
decisions.source: VISION §6 Explore and find earlier learning

decisions.question: Is grouping #49's 86 user stories into the LJ-REVIEW, LJ-RECORDS, LJ-REPAIR and LJ-SCHEDULE families (each citing story numbers) the right granularity, or should each #49 story get its own ID before its implementation is planned?

The spec's initial live exercise allows only teaching, question and planning tools, while #49 acceptance requires a live run with normal functionality enabled (background reader, graph processing). Confirm these are separate authorizations and that #49's live harness needs its own approval.
How are cross-device continuity and synchronization delivered (native/web, sync)? The vision leaves these open.

stories.title: Start learning from a goal and probe prerequisites
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I state what I want to learn and the tutor finds my prerequisite boundary before teaching, so teaching starts from what I actually understand.

happy: A goal leads to probing questions; a successful probe_done result (not merely an attempted call) is saved and the session moves to planning.
alternative: A learner who already knows much of the material reaches the handoff with fewer probing turns.
failureOrReturn: A failed or invalid probe_done does not move the session into teaching.

claims: synthetic goal persisted
successful probe_done persisted

stories.title: Start from a goal together with a reference
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I supply a book or other reference with my goal, so the tutor uses its notation, jargon and required knowledge while building my own path.

happy: The tutor reads the supplied reference and its explanations use the reference's notation for the goal.
alternative: The tutor teaches in a different order from the book when that suits the learner; no fixed lesson sequence is required.
failureOrReturn: An unreadable or missing reference is reported to the learner rather than silently ignored or invented.

stories.availabilityBasis: read/pdf_* tools and file attachments exist; faithful book extraction is follow-up #36
claims: no reference-alignment check exists yet

stories.title: Plan, teach, respond to uncertainty and retry
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I get a teaching plan, learn step by step, and when I am wrong or unsure I get feedback and can try again, so a mistake becomes part of learning.

happy: A validated plan is saved; an uncertain answer receives feedback; the retry is saved as a separate attempt.
alternative: The tutor may explain directly instead of asking for discovery when the learner asks or seems stuck.
failureOrReturn: A wrong answer does not end the step or erase the earlier attempt.

claims: validated plan persisted
scripted feedback and retry persisted, not tutor accuracy

stories.title: Revise the teaching plan as learning proceeds
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, when the route is wrong or misses a step, the tutor revises the plan, so the plan keeps serving my goal instead of a fixed syllabus.

happy: After the learner points out a missing step, the presented plan shows the revised route and earlier messages are unchanged.
alternative: The tutor revises the plan on its own after new learner evidence.
failureOrReturn: An invalid revision is rejected and the previous plan stays presented.

claims: learner-prompted scripted rewrite only; whether the tutor revises at the right moments needs LJ-TUTOR

stories.title: Ask for explanation, help or a side question while learning
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I can ask for an explanation, a hint or a side question at any point, so I get help without losing my place.

happy: A side question is answered and the plan position and earlier work are unchanged.
alternative: The tutor answers briefly and returns to the current step, or offers to revise the plan.
failureOrReturn: A request for help is not recorded as independent success on the current step.

stories.title: Read, see and experiment with the material
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I get readable mathematics, useful diagrams and interactive demonstrations, so I can study, experiment and do my own work.

happy: Mathematics renders readably, a requested diagram or demo appears in the conversation and stays there on reopen.
alternative: The tutor chooses text when a visual would not help.
failureOrReturn: A failed diagram/demo job is shown as failed without breaking the conversation.

stories.availabilityBasis: visual/demo jobs, mermaid and math rendering
claims: presentation quality also needs owner UX judgment (V-7)

stories.title: Work in typed, spoken, handwritten or mixed form
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I can answer by typing, speaking, writing by hand, or sending photos and PDFs, so I can work in the form that suits the problem and device.

happy: Spoken, handwritten and typed work reaches the tutor and the original work is preserved in the record.
alternative: Mixed input (handwriting plus speech) is submitted as one attempt.
failureOrReturn: Uncertain interpretation is clarified before assessment; a failed transcription keeps the original work.

stories.availabilityBasis: dictation, notebook/handwriting and learner images exist; chat image attachments are in an open PR
claims: mobile browser checks cover input plumbing, not assessment of interpreted work

stories.title: Keep continuing mathematical working in a notebook
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, my mathematical working lives in a notebook beside the conversation, spans several questions and topics, and I can share a snapshot of it with the tutor.

happy: Working written for one question is still in the notebook for the next; sharing a snapshot gives the tutor that working without moving it into the conversation.
alternative: The learner refers to a numbered line or selected expression when asking the tutor about a step.
failureOrReturn: Reopening the session keeps the notebook working; a failed snapshot share keeps the working and reports the failure.

claims: device routing (canvas on tablet, equation notebook on phone) is a settings choice, not a separate story

stories.title: Practise with graduated help after a wrong answer
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, when my practice answer is wrong I get the smallest useful help and keep working until I solve it or choose to stop, and the record shows that I needed help.

happy: A posed problem hides its committed solution; a wrong answer gets feedback while the problem stays open; a corrected answer concludes as helped success with the help recorded and the solution revealed; the next problem waits for the learner's go-ahead.
alternative: An independent correct first answer concludes as solved with no help recorded.
failureOrReturn: The learner explicitly ends the problem; it concludes without being counted as success.

claims: scripted outcome and rung persisted and solution hidden until conclusion; hint size and verdict quality need LJ-TUTOR

stories.title: Return to an unfinished practice problem
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, if I stop mid-problem and come back, the same problem and my earlier attempts are still there, so stopping is not failure.

happy: Reopening shows the same open problem and earlier attempt, the solution stays hidden, and the problem can still be completed.
alternative: The learner discusses the problem before continuing it.
failureOrReturn: Stopping records no outcome. Unsubmitted drafts across reload are not yet durable (I49 story 42).

stories.availabilityBasis: open problem is derived from saved messages (activeProblemOf); durable drafts are #49 scope
claims: submitted work and open problem survive same-process reopen; unsubmitted draft durability not covered

stories.title: Take an optional focused drill as a separate activity
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I can choose a focused drill on a specific difficulty that stays separate from my main learning, so repetition does not distort ordinary mixed practice.

happy: A learner-created drill keeps its drill identity through help and conclusion; other sessions are unchanged.
alternative: The drill uses a mental model to scaffold the work rather than pure repetition.
failureOrReturn: Helped success in a drill is not recorded as independent success.

claims: created through the same chats API the New drill screen uses; drill method quality needs LJ-TUTOR

stories.title: Tutor suggests a drill the learner may accept
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, the tutor can suggest a drill when it sees a need, and I choose whether to do it.

happy: After repeated unit-conversion slips the tutor suggests a drill; accepting opens it with that context.
alternative: The learner declines and teaching continues unchanged.
failureOrReturn: No drill starts without the learner's choice.

stories.availabilityBasis: no prescription-to-drill handoff found; the transition design is open in #15
claims: blocked on D-4

stories.title: Close, reopen and continue with earlier work accessible
stories.learnerGoal: As a returning learner, my earlier messages, plan and position are still there and I can continue, so stopping costs nothing.

happy: After reopen, earlier messages and the plan are visible and a continuation is appended without changing them.
alternative: The learner returns through the session list instead of a direct link.
failureOrReturn: A restart of the app (cross-process) preserves the same history; not yet verified.

claims: same-process continuity only
earlier messages and plan survive reopen

stories.title: Find earlier explanations, sources and work
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I can search across sessions for an earlier explanation, source, attempt or feedback and return to it in context.
sources: VISION §6 Explore and find earlier learning

happy: Searching for a term finds the earlier explanation in another session and opens it at that point.
alternative: Finding within the open session highlights matches in place.
failureOrReturn: No match is shown as no match, not as an empty history.

stories.availabilityBasis: session list search and in-session find exist; cross-session content search not found

stories.title: Move between teaching, practice, drills and review without losing purpose
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I can move between activities and come back, with each keeping its purpose, work and history.

happy: Leaving teaching for a drill and returning preserves the teaching position and the drill's separate record.
alternative: Decided in #15.
failureOrReturn: Decided in #15.

stories.availabilityBasis: sessions are separate and resumable; no designed transitions
claims: blocked on D-4

stories.title: Review earlier learning
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I revisit earlier understanding and application after a delay through varied fresh activities, so I retain what I learned.

happy: See the child stories LJ-REVIEW-ENTRY, LJ-REVIEW-WORK and LJ-REVIEW-SESSION.
alternative: Review fits a time constraint the learner gives in conversation.
failureOrReturn: When nothing can start, the reason is explained.

stories.availabilityBasis: no Review mode or capability records found; specified by #49
claims: parent story; #49 requires its own approved implementation plan and live harness

stories.title: Enter Review directly and resume or select due work
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, one Review entry resumes my unfinished work or picks useful due material for my goals.

happy: Review resumes an unfinished problem, otherwise selects due, ready material across active goals.
alternative: A conversational time limit shapes the session; already-ready work is available during background catch-up.
failureOrReturn: With nothing eligible, the learner sees whether nothing is due, repair is pending or records are not ready; explicit pauses are respected.

stories.title: Work varied review problems with honest capability assessment
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, review exercises explanation, derivation, calculation and application, assessing each capability separately and honestly.

happy: A circuit problem keeps its figure, uses Practice's adaptive help, and records separate capability outcomes when help was needed for one part.
alternative: A local weakness gets a smaller component follow-up instead of repeating the whole task.
failureOrReturn: Slips, clarifications and real gaps are interpreted in context rather than as identical misses.

stories.title: Rate, discuss, pause and finish Review on my terms
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I can rate or skip, discuss concluded work, pause mid-problem and finish when I choose, and a completed Review stays discussable.

happy: Rating or explicit Skip precedes the tutor's judgment; Next waits; Finish is honored; drafts and ratings survive reload.
alternative: Ordinary Review works with temporary calibration disabled.
failureOrReturn: Stopping mid-problem pauses it intact; new exercises after completion start a fresh Review.

stories.title: Review timing follows genuine work and corrections
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, review timing reflects my real substantive work, counts connected help as one attempt, and updates when an assessment is corrected.

happy: A qualifying early success informs timing; an accepted correction updates the schedule and keeps its history.
alternative: Late-discovered earlier work is reconciled chronologically.
failureOrReturn: Insufficient component work does not postpone broader review; a timing update does not interrupt a problem underway.

claims: synthetic scheduler probes validate mechanics, not retention

stories.title: Check understanding on demand
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I can ask to be checked on selected studied topics to find out what I can independently explain or apply, and the results join my learning history.

happy: Choosing studied topics yields independent checks whose results are saved as learner evidence.
alternative: Mechanics and feedback timing as decided under D-5.
failureOrReturn: A visited plan node or encountered proposition is never reported as a passed check.

stories.availabilityBasis: practice from picked graph propositions exists; no distinct check activity or shared evidence history
claims: requires approved assessment expectations; visited is not mastery
blocked on D-5

stories.title: Repair a confirmed understanding gap through Teaching
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, a real understanding gap found in review leads to an arranged Teaching session I choose when to enter, while other review continues.

happy: A supported gap holds only the affected capability; opening the prepared session starts the owed first turn; supported reasoning restores readiness.
alternative: Ordinary retrieval difficulty stays within Practice; a matching unfinished repair is reused.
failureOrReturn: A recurrence after repair opens a new episode with earlier context; opening or finishing Teaching alone is not repair.

stories.title: Lasting, honest learning records
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, my teaching and practice contribute to lasting, dated capability records that distinguish what I encountered, did with help, did independently and retained later.

happy: New and earlier Teaching produce dated capability records with scope, help and uncertainty preserved.
alternative: Intended capabilities are recorded as unassessed until evidence exists; shared capabilities have one history across goals.
failureOrReturn: Old evidence is treated as uncertain freshness, not as a gap; graph propositions and plan landmarks are not evidence about the learner.

stories.availabilityBasis: learner evidence exists only inside session records (practice outcomes, probe assessment)

stories.title: Inspect and correct what the app thinks I know
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I can inspect conclusions about my learning with their evidence and history, challenge them, and have accepted corrections take effect with reasons kept.

happy: From navigation or review feedback, a record shows summary, scope, dates and original-work links; a challenge with evidence leads to an accepted correction.
alternative: Disagreement that is not accepted is kept but does not change the record.
failureOrReturn: A correction revises history without manufacturing a new attempt.

stories.title: Background record processing survives interruptions
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, background processing recovers after restart without duplicates, shows paused, blocked and failed states, and never fabricates or erases history.

happy: Records are available before graph linking completes; restart resumes processing without duplicates.
alternative: The learner pauses and resumes processing.
failureOrReturn: Missing sources are shown honestly; permission or configuration blockers are distinct from failures.

stories.title: Continue toward the goal using learner evidence
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, teaching, practice and later study form one coherent view of what I understand and need next, so the tutor continues from my actual evidence.

happy: After a gap shown in practice, later teaching addresses it without the learner restating it.
alternative: Evidence from a check or review changes the next teaching focus.
failureOrReturn: A saved conversation alone is not reported as evidence-guided adaptation.

stories.availabilityBasis: cross-session evidence reuse is a stated fork extension; not established
claims: saved conversation alone does not establish evidence-guided adaptation

stories.title: Explore demonstrated understanding alongside connections between ideas
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I can see demonstrated understanding and uncertainty next to how ideas connect, to decide what to explore or revisit.
sources: VISION §6 Explore and find earlier learning

happy: Pending D-6 domain alignment.
alternative: Pending D-6.
failureOrReturn: Subject content is never presented as learner mastery.

stories.availabilityBasis: knowledge graph view exists; no learner-evidence layer
claims: blocked on D-6

stories.title: Teaching and imported notes build the shared knowledge graph
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, propositions and reasoning chains from teaching and my imported notes are kept with their origins, so later learning can connect to them.

happy: After teaching, extracted propositions appear in the graph with their source session.
alternative: Imported notes produce propositions with the note as origin.
failureOrReturn: Extraction off or failing is shown explicitly; the graph is never labeled as mastery.

stories.title: Interruptions and failures do not lose learning work
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, stopping a running reply, a provider failure or a missing model setup is explained and my earlier work stays intact.

happy: Aborting a running turn keeps earlier messages and lets the learner continue.
alternative: A provider error is shown and the learner can resend.
failureOrReturn: Missing configuration explains what to set up; no silent API-billing fallback.

stories.title: Continue one journey on whatever device is available
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I continue the same learning on desktop, phone or iPad with activities and inputs suited to each.

happy: Work started on desktop continues on an iPad Home Screen app with the same history.
alternative: The phone suits spoken short answers and the iPad written derivations.
failureOrReturn: An unavailable target is reported blocked, never passed.

stories.availabilityBasis: web app on phone/iPad and Electron desktop exist; synchronization is open
claims: blocked on D-3 and D-9; mobile emulation is not physical-device evidence

stories.title: Back up and restore my learning history
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, I can back up and restore all learning history and unfinished work, including original attempts, feedback and corrections.

happy: A backup restored into a fresh data directory reproduces sessions, attempts and unfinished work.
alternative: Restoring onto existing data is explicit about what changes.
failureOrReturn: A corrupt or partial backup is refused without damaging current data.

stories.availabilityBasis: no backup/restore feature found; data is plain files under LH_DATA_DIR
claims: no ticket exists yet

stories.title: Independent subject and teaching evaluation
stories.learnerGoal: As a learner, the tutor's subject content is correct and its teaching follows the approved approach: probe the boundary, check each step, choose discovery or explanation, give minimal graduated help.

happy: Against an approved key, every required expectation in a live multi-turn run passes per turn purpose.
alternative: Valid alternative conversations and explanations pass; there is no exact-transcript oracle.
failureOrReturn: One material subject error or required teaching violation fails the scenario; uncertain judgments stay unverified; a reached cap is incomplete.

stories.availabilityBasis: tutor exists; its quality is what this evaluates
claims: draft linear-algebra key v0.5.1 (verification/learning/keys/la-eigen-2x2) awaits owner approval under D-1
calibration and an enforceable live adapter still need approval
blocked on D-1, D-2 and D-8
